headlines.title: EU President to Skip Serbia and Bosnia on Balkan Tour
Bosnia Seizes 1.1 Tons of Synthetic Drugs Worth Up to €33 Million
Fining Bosnia’s Parties for Campaign Violations Won’t Deter Them, Expert Warns
Slovakia Seeks to Overturn Conviction of Fugitive Who Claimed Asylum in Bosnia
Bosnia’s Elections Offer New Technologies, But Old Politics

brief.text:
SITUATION NOW
The EU President will skip Serbia and Bosnia on a Balkan tour. [1]
Bosnia seized 1.1 tons of synthetic drugs worth up to €33 million. [2]
An expert warns that fining Bosnia’s parties for campaign violations will not deter them. [3]
Slovakia seeks to overturn the conviction of a fugitive who claimed asylum in Bosnia. [4]
Bosnia’s elections offer new technologies, but old politics. [5]

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA
The EU President's decision to skip Bosnia may signal reduced high-level diplomatic engagement with the country. [1]
The large drug seizure indicates significant illicit trafficking activity in Bosnia. [2]

KEY RISKS
Fining parties for campaign violations is unlikely to deter them, according to an expert. [3]
Slovakia's effort to overturn the conviction of a fugitive in Bosnia could create legal or diplomatic friction. [4]

WATCH ITEMS
The outcome of Slovakia's attempt to overturn the fugitive's conviction in Bosnia remains unresolved. [4]
Whether new election technologies will overcome old political practices in Bosnia is uncertain. [5]
